scope: Read-only privacy, terminal export closure, creator-side exact source byte hash, unknown/retry/inflight accounting, sticky export failure and deterministic legacy-policy parity review. No implementation integration or current ledger access.
verified_contracts: Export events use a fixed purpose/status whitelist and scalar finite/count metadata; free-text errors/prompts/responses/headers/model names/environment/addresses/absolute paths are excluded.

Missing or invalid counts stay null, primary missing value does not silently fall back to alias, retries retain known sums with incomplete total usage; in-flight authorizations are visible and cannot yield usage_complete.

Only own creating RunBudget reads its newly created source ledger; exact persisted bytes are SHA256-bound. Closed export is attempted after source flush at actual context exit; failed/interrupted solver status is distinct from usage completeness.
Destination and temporary files use exclusive ordinal creation under an ordinary checked parent; existing artifacts are preserved and write failure stays sticky across later successful exports.

Original snapshot and authorization control logic remain in place; saved deterministic parity fixture compares exact legacy snapshot/admission outcomes, not measured wall-time overhead or provider billing.
limits: New file I/O has unmeasured real wall-time cost charged to the future common clock; unchanged deterministic clock fixtures do not prove zero timing overhead.

Future supervisor must independently require normal readability, closed/source_ledger_closed/export_integrity_ok/usage_complete, allowed terminal status, valid arithmetic and finite cap bounds; parent-reported counters cannot replace a missing export.
Source hash is a creator-side byte binding, not independent access to the private source ledger or provider billing proof. No historical inaccessible ledger is retrofitted.
Registry/flat-build/full release/live destination gate remain pending; canonical and active tm1 source stay frozen.
